nodes.title: Decline of Mughal Empire & Rise of Regional Powers
prelimsNote: After Aurangzeb (d. 1707): weak successors, jagirdari crisis, Nadir Shah's invasion (1739), Ahmad Shah Abdali's raids (Third Battle of Panipat 1761, Marathas defeated).
Successor states: Hyderabad (Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah, 1724), Bengal (Murshid Quli Khan), Awadh (Saadat Khan) — nominal Mughal allegiance.
Regional/new states: Marathas under the Peshwas, Mysore (Haidar Ali, Tipu), Sikhs (Ranjit Singh), Rohillas, Jats.
Arcot, Mysore and Rohilkhand were 18th-century regional kingdoms (UPSC 2021).

nodes.title: Advent of Europeans & British Conquest of India
prelimsNote: Arrival order: Portuguese (Vasco da Gama, Calicut 1498) → Dutch → English → Danes → French.

Dutch set up factories on the east coast on lands granted by Gajapati rulers; Albuquerque captured Goa from the Bijapur Sultanate (1510); English factory at Madras on land leased from a Vijayanagara representative (UPSC 2022).
Plassey 1757 (Siraj-ud-Daulah, Mir Jafar) and Buxar 1764 (Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula, Shah Alam II) → Treaty of Allahabad 1765: Diwani of Bengal, Bihar, Orissa.
Carnatic Wars ended French ambitions — Battle of Wandiwash 1760.
EIC factories: Surat (1613), Masulipatnam, Madras (Fort St George 1639), Bombay (from Portuguese dowry 1661), Calcutta (1690) — UPSC 2021.

nodes.title: Governors-General & Colonial Administration till 1857
prelimsNote: Warren Hastings: Ring-Fence policy, Regulating Act; Cornwallis: Permanent Settlement 1793, Cornwallis Code; Wellesley: Subsidiary Alliance, Fort William College (1800).
Subsidiary Alliance: Indian ruler kept a British force at his own cost and a Resident — it did NOT aim to secure a fixed income for the Company (UPSC 2018).
Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse: Satara (1848), Jaitpur, Sambalpur, Udaipur, Jhansi, Nagpur; Awadh annexed in 1856 on grounds of misgovernance (not lapse).
Bentinck: abolition of Sati (1829), first Governor-General of India (1833); Hardinge, Dalhousie: railways (1853), telegraph.

nodes.title: Tribal Revolts Against British Rule
prelimsNote: Santhal Hool (1855–56, Sidhu & Kanhu) → Santhal Pargana created, special laws for Santhals (UPSC 2018).
Munda Ulgulan (1899–1900, Birsa Munda) — 'great tumult' in Chota Nagpur (UPSC 2020).
Other revolts: Kol (1831–32, Buddho Bhagat), Khasi (Tirot Sing), Rampa (1922–24, Alluri Sitarama Raju), Bhil, Koya.
Colonial forest laws and the zamindari/moneylender nexus disrupted tribal economies (UPSC 2011).
Bhil Seva Mandal (1922) was founded by Amritlal Vithaldas Thakkar (Thakkar Bapa).

nodes.title: Peasant Movements & Civil Rebellions in Colonial India
prelimsNote: Indigo Revolt (1859–60) in Bengal; Dinabandhu Mitra's play Nil Darpan; Indigo Commission 1860.
Pabna Agrarian League (1873); Deccan Riots (1875) → Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act 1879.
Tebhaga (1946, Bengal): sharecroppers demanded two-thirds of the harvest (UPSC 2013).
Champaran (1917): against the tinkathia system — Gandhi's first satyagraha in India (UPSC 2011, 2018).
Natural indigo declined with synthetic dyes from Germany (UPSC 2020); Bardoli (1928) gave Vallabhbhai Patel the title 'Sardar'.

nodes.title: Revolt of 1857 — Causes, Course & Significance
prelimsNote: Immediate cause: greased cartridges of the Enfield rifle; General Service Enlistment Act 1856 and Doctrine of Lapse added grievances.
Leaders: Delhi — Bahadur Shah Zafar, Bakht Khan; Kanpur — Nana Saheb, Tantia Tope; Lucknow — Begum Hazrat Mahal; Jhansi — Rani Lakshmibai; Bihar — Kunwar Singh; Faizabad — Maulvi Ahmadullah.
British commanders: Nicholson (Delhi), Colin Campbell (Lucknow), Hugh Rose (Jhansi).
Outcome: Government of India Act 1858 and Queen Victoria's Proclamation — Crown rule, no further annexation of Indian States (UPSC 2014).
Never asked directly in recent UPSC Prelims — a likely gap area.

nodes.title: 19th Century Social Reform Movements — Ram Mohan Roy, Vidyasagar
prelimsNote: Raja Ram Mohan Roy: Atmiya Sabha (1814), Brahmo Sabha (1828), campaign leading to Sati abolition (1829).
Brahmo split: Adi Brahmo Samaj (Debendranath Tagore) vs Brahmo Samaj of India (Keshub Chandra Sen, 1866) — UPSC 2012, 2016.
Vidyasagar: Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act 1856; Derozio and Young Bengal.
Hindu Female School (Calcutta, 1849) was founded by J.E.D. Bethune with Vidyasagar's support (UPSC 2021).

nodes.title: Reforms in Western India — Ranade, Phule, Ambedkar
prelimsNote: Prarthana Samaj (1867, Atmaram Pandurang; M.G. Ranade); Gopal Hari Deshmukh 'Lokahitawadi'.
Jyotirao Phule: Satyashodhak Samaj (1873), Gulamgiri; school for girls (1848) with Savitribai (UPSC 2016).
Rakhmabai's case (1880s) led to the Age of Consent Act 1891 (UPSC 2020).
Ambedkar: Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924), Mahad Satyagraha (1927), Mooknayak; parties — Independent Labour Party (1936), Scheduled Castes Federation (1942) — UPSC 2012.

nodes.title: Reforms in South India — Periyar, Narayana Guru
prelimsNote: Self-Respect Movement (1925) founded by E.V. Ramasamy 'Periyar' (UPSC 2021).
Sree Narayana Guru: SNDP Yogam (1903), Aruvippuram (1888) — 'One caste, one religion, one God'.
Vaikom Satyagraha (1924–25) for temple-road access; Guruvayur Satyagraha (1931–32).
Justice Party (1916) — non-Brahmin movement in Madras.

nodes.title: Caste Movements in Northern & Eastern India
prelimsNote: Ad-Dharm (Punjab, 1920s), Matua (Bengal, Harichand Thakur), Satnami (Chhattisgarh).
All India Anti-Untouchability League (1932, Gandhi), soon renamed Harijan Sevak Sangh — UPSC 2019 paired it correctly with Gandhi.
Depressed Classes Mission (1906, V.R. Shinde) worked for untouchables in western India.
Trap: the Self-Respect and SNDP movements are southern, not northern.

nodes.title: Rise of Indian Nationalism & Indian National Congress
prelimsNote: Pre-Congress bodies: Landholders' Society (1838), British Indian Association (1851, Radhakanta Deb), East India Association (1866, Naoroji), Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870), Indian Association (1876, Surendranath Banerjee) — UPSC 2017.
INC founded 1885 at Bombay; A.O. Hume; first president W.C. Bonnerjee; 'Safety-valve' theory.
British Committee of the INC was set up in London (1889) — UPSC 2011.
First women presidents: Annie Besant (1917), Sarojini Naidu (1925) — UPSC 2015; Ilbert Bill controversy (1883) — UPSC 2013.
National Social Conference (1887, Ranade) addressed social reform alongside the INC (UPSC 2012).

nodes.title: Early Nationalists — Moderates vs Extremists
prelimsNote: Moderates' methods: petitions, prayers, protests, constitutional agitation — not boycott or passive resistance (UPSC 2021).
Economic critique: Dadabhai Naoroji ('Poverty and Un-British Rule'), R.C. Dutt, M.G. Ranade (UPSC 2015).
Extremists (Lal–Bal–Pal, Aurobindo): swaraj, swadeshi, boycott, national education.
Surat Split 1907: disagreement over the Swadeshi/boycott programme and presidency (Rash Behari Ghosh) — UPSC 2015, 2016.

nodes.title: Revolutionary & Militant Nationalism — Bhagat Singh, Gadar Movement
prelimsNote: Ghadar Party (1913, San Francisco): Lala Har Dayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna; Barindra Kumar Ghosh was NOT a Ghadar member, Rash Behari Bose was (UPSC 2022).
Anushilan Samiti and Jugantar (Bengal), Abhinav Bharat (Savarkar); Komagata Maru (1914).
HRA → HSRA (1928, Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad); Kakori (1925); Central Assembly bomb (1929); Bhagat Singh hanged 23 March 1931.
Chittagong Armoury Raid (1930, Surya Sen); Berlin Committee (1915).

nodes.title: Home Rule Movement — Tilak & Besant
prelimsNote: Tilak's Home Rule League (April 1916, Belgaum) — Maharashtra, Karnataka, CP, Berar; Besant's (Sept 1916, Madras) — rest of India.
Besant's papers: New India and Commonweal; she was the first woman INC president (1917) — UPSC 2013.
Lucknow Pact 1916: Congress–League agreement accepting separate electorates; Moderates and Extremists reunited.
Swarajya Sabha (Gandhi's renaming of the Home Rule League, 1920) — UPSC 2018.

nodes.title: Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22)
prelimsNote: Launched after the Rowlatt Act (1919), Jallianwala Bagh (13 April 1919) and the Khilafat issue; approved at Calcutta special session, ratified at Nagpur (1920).
Programme: surrender of titles, boycott of courts, schools, councils and foreign cloth; swadeshi, national schools.
Withdrawn after Chauri Chaura (4 Feb 1922) — Bardoli resolution.
Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919) was the first all-India mass struggle under Gandhi (UPSC 2015).
Swarajists (C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru, 1923) vs No-Changers (Rajagopalachari, Patel).

nodes.title: Civil Disobedience Movement & Dandi March
prelimsNote: Dandi March: 12 March–6 April 1930 from Sabarmati; salt laws broken.
Vedaranyam salt march (Tamil Nadu) led by C. Rajagopalachari (UPSC 2015); Dharasana (Sarojini Naidu); Khudai Khidmatgar (Abdul Ghaffar Khan) in NWFP.
Gandhi–Irwin Pact (March 1931): release of non-violent prisoners, Congress to attend the Second RTC — it did NOT accept Dominion Status or Purna Swaraj (UPSC 2020).
Karachi Session 1931 (Patel): resolutions on Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme.

nodes.title: Round Table Conferences & Communal Award
prelimsNote: First RTC (1930) boycotted by Congress; Gandhi attended only the Second (1931); Third (1932).
Communal Award (1932, Ramsay MacDonald): separate electorates extended to Depressed Classes.
Gandhi's fast at Yerwada → Poona Pact (1932): reserved seats for Depressed Classes within joint electorates (UPSC 2012).
Ambedkar attended all three RTCs.

nodes.title: Quit India Movement (1942)
prelimsNote: Resolution at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 8 August 1942 — 'Do or Die' (UPSC 2021).
Triggered by the failure of the Cripps Mission and the Japanese threat (UPSC 2013).
Underground: Aruna Asaf Ali, Usha Mehta's Congress Radio (UPSC 2011), Ram Manohar Lohia, J.P. Narayan.
Parallel governments: Ballia (Chittu Pandey), Tamluk (Jatiya Sarkar), Satara (Prati Sarkar).

nodes.title: Subhas Chandra Bose & Indian National Army
prelimsNote: INA first formed by Mohan Singh (1942); revived by Bose; Provisional Government of Free India (Singapore, Oct 1943).
INA trials at Red Fort (1945): Shah Nawaz Khan, P.K. Sehgal, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon — defended by Bhulabhai Desai, Tej Bahadur Sapru, Nehru (UPSC 2021).
RIN Mutiny (Feb 1946) in Bombay followed the INA trials.
Bose was Congress president at Haripura (1938) and Tripuri (1939); founded the Forward Bloc.

nodes.title: Trade Union & Peasant Movements — Pre-Independence
prelimsNote: AITUC (1920; first president Lala Lajpat Rai); Trade Union Act 1926; Trade Disputes Act 1929 (UPSC 2017).
N.M. Lokhande pioneered labour organisation (Bombay Mill Hands' Association) — Factories Act 1881 did not fix wages (UPSC 2017).
Congress Socialist Party (1934, J.P. Narayan, Acharya Narendra Dev) — UPSC 2015; All India Kisan Sabha (1936).
Hind Mazdoor Sabha (1948) was founded by socialists (UPSC 2018).

nodes.title: Partition of India — Causes, Communalism & Human Cost
prelimsNote: Muslim League's Lahore Resolution (1940) demanded separate states; Direct Action Day (16 Aug 1946).
C.R. Formula (1944) and Gandhi–Jinnah talks failed; Wavell Plan & Simla Conference (1945).
Radcliffe Line: Sir Cyril Radcliffe chaired both Boundary Commissions (Punjab and Bengal) — UPSC 2014.
Indian Independence Act 1947: two dominions, end of paramountcy.

nodes.title: Cabinet Mission, Mountbatten Plan & Transfer of Power
prelimsNote: Cabinet Mission (1946): Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, A.V. Alexander — rejected Pakistan, proposed groups A/B/C and a Constituent Assembly elected by provincial assemblies.
Interim Government (Sept 1946) headed by Nehru.
Mountbatten (3 June) Plan 1947: partition, independence brought forward to 15 August 1947.
UPSC 2017 asked the chronology of 1940s events (Quit India, RIN mutiny, Simla Conference).

nodes.title: British Economic Policies & Their Exploitation
prelimsNote: Drain of wealth (Dadabhai Naoroji, R.C. Dutt): Home Charges — pensions, interest on debt, salaries paid in England (UPSC 2011, 2012).
De-industrialisation after the Industrial Revolution: Indian handicrafts declined and India became a raw-material supplier (UPSC 2020).
Commercialisation of agriculture: cash crops (indigo, cotton, opium, jute) for export (UPSC 2018).
Bengal's exports in the early 19th century included raw cotton, raw silk, indigo, sugar, opium (UPSC 2018).
Famine Commissions: Campbell (1866), Strachey (1880, Famine Code), Lyall (1897), MacDonnell (1901).

nodes.title: Christian Missionaries & Social Impact
prelimsNote: Charter Act 1813 allowed missionaries to work in India.
Serampore Mission (Danish territory, 1800): William Carey, Marshman, Ward — printing press and vernacular translations.
Missionaries in the colonial period worked in education, health and among tribal communities (UPSC 2021).
Charles Grant is called the father of modern education in India.

nodes.title: Role of Press & Literature in Freedom Struggle
prelimsNote: Hicky's Bengal Gazette (1780) was India's first newspaper; Metcalfe (1835) 'liberator of the Indian press'.
Vernacular Press Act 1878 (Lytton, 'Gagging Act') repealed by Ripon in 1882; Amrita Bazar Patrika turned English overnight.
Papers: Kesari & Mahratta (Tilak), Young India & Harijan (Gandhi), Al-Hilal (Azad), Bengalee (S.N. Banerjee), Vital-Vidhvansak (Gopal Baba Walangkar, for untouchables — UPSC 2020).
Desher Katha (Sakharam Ganesh Deuskar) on the drain of wealth was banned (UPSC 2020); Songs from Prison is Gandhi's translation of Upanishadic hymns (UPSC 2021).
Lala Lajpat Rai wrote 'Unhappy India' and founded the Punjabee (UPSC 2018).

newNodesToCreate.title: North Indian & Muslim Reform Movements — Arya Samaj, Ramakrishna, Aligarh & Deoband
prelimsNote: Arya Samaj (1875, Bombay; Dayanand Saraswati): 'Go back to the Vedas', Satyarth Prakash, Shuddhi; DAV vs Gurukul (Kangri) split.
Ramakrishna Mission (1897, Vivekananda) — Chicago Parliament of Religions (1893); Theosophical Society in India (Adyar, 1886; Annie Besant).
Aligarh Movement (Sir Syed Ahmad Khan) — MAO College 1875; Deoband (1866) — orthodox; Ahmadiyya (Mirza Ghulam Ahmad); Faraizi (Haji Shariatullah).
Chronology questions (UPSC 2018) mix reformist events — memorise founding years.

newNodesToCreate.title: Partition of Bengal, Swadeshi & Surat Split (1905–1911)
prelimsNote: Partition of Bengal announced by Curzon (1905); annulled in 1911 by Hardinge, capital shifted to Delhi (UPSC 2014).
Swadeshi & boycott (UPSC 2016): Bengal Chemical Swadeshi Stores (P.C. Ray), National Council of Education (1906), Vande Mataram, Amar Sonar Bangla.
Outcomes (UPSC 2019): revival of indigenous artisan crafts and a boost to national education — the movement extended beyond Bengal.
7 August 1905 boycott resolution at Calcutta Town Hall → 7 August is National Handloom Day (2015) — UPSC 2023.
Surat Split (1907) and the Muslim League's founding (1906, Dhaka) followed.

newNodesToCreate.title: Gandhi's Early Satyagrahas, Rowlatt Act & Jallianwala Bagh
prelimsNote: Gandhi returned on 9 Jan 1915; first public appearance in India: the Banaras Hindu University opening (1916) — UPSC 2021.
Champaran (1917, tinkathia, Rajkumar Shukla): showed peasant mobilisation through satyagraha and the issues of indigo cultivators (UPSC 2018).
Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918): first hunger strike; Kheda (1918): first non-cooperation (revenue remission).
Rowlatt Act 1919 ('no dalil, no vakil, no appeal') → Jallianwala Bagh, 13 April 1919 (Dyer); Tagore renounced his knighthood; Hunter Committee.
Gandhi's influences include Ruskin's 'Unto This Last' (UPSC 2011).

newNodesToCreate.title: Constitutional Politics 1922–1931 — Swarajists, Simon Commission, Nehru Report & Lahore Session
prelimsNote: Swaraj Party (1923, C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru) entered councils to wreck them from within.
Nehru Report (1928): Dominion Status, fundamental rights, joint electorates; Jinnah's 14 Points (1929) in response.
Lahore Session (1929, Jawaharlal Nehru): Purna Swaraj; 26 January 1930 observed as Independence Day (UPSC 2012, 2014).
Congress ministries formed in 1937 resigned in 1939 over India's unilateral entry into WWII (UPSC 2012).

newNodesToCreate.title: World War II Phase — August Offer, Individual Satyagraha & Cripps Mission
prelimsNote: August Offer (1940, Linlithgow): Dominion Status as objective, expanded Executive Council — rejected by Congress.
Individual Satyagraha (1940–41): Vinoba Bhave first, Nehru second.

Cripps Mission (1942): Dominion Status after the war; Constituent Assembly elected by provincial assemblies and nominees of princely States; provinces could opt out — Gandhi: 'post-dated cheque' (UPSC 2016, 2022).
Its failure led to the Quit India Movement (UPSC 2013).

newNodesToCreate.title: Constitutional Acts I — Regulating Act 1773 to Government of India Act 1858
prelimsNote: Regulating Act 1773: Governor of Bengal → Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings); Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774).
Pitt's India Act 1784: Board of Control → 'double government'; Charter Act 1793 renewed the monopoly for 20 years.
Charter Act 1813: ended the trade monopoly except tea and China trade; ₹1 lakh for education; missionaries allowed — it did NOT put Indian revenues under Parliament's control (UPSC 2019).
Charter Act 1833: Governor-General of India (Bentinck); Company's commercial functions ended; Law Member (Macaulay) — UPSC 2023.
Charter Act 1853: open competition for civil services; GoI Act 1858 and Queen Victoria's Proclamation: Crown rule, Secretary of State, no annexation of Indian States (UPSC 2014).

newNodesToCreate.title: Constitutional Acts II — Indian Councils Acts to Government of India Act 1935
prelimsNote: Indian Councils Act 1861: portfolio system, ordinance power; 1892: indirect elections, budget discussion.
Morley–Minto (1909): separate electorates for Muslims; S.P. Sinha first Indian on the Viceroy's Executive Council.
Montagu–Chelmsford / GoI Act 1919: dyarchy in provinces (UPSC 2017) — Reserved subjects: administration of justice, police, land revenue (UPSC 2022); bicameral Centre.
GoI Act 1935: provincial autonomy, dyarchy at the Centre (never implemented), Federal Court (1937); residuary powers with the Governor-General (UPSC 2018).
Simon Commission (1927) was all-white and boycotted; Lala Lajpat Rai died after the lathi charge (UPSC 2013).

newNodesToCreate.title: Land Revenue Systems — Permanent, Ryotwari & Mahalwari
prelimsNote: Permanent Settlement (1793, Cornwallis): zamindars as owners, fixed revenue — Bengal, Bihar, Orissa.
Ryotwari: Thomas Munro and Alexander Read in Madras and Bombay — direct settlement with cultivators; Cornwallis had nothing to do with it (UPSC 2017).
Mahalwari (Holt Mackenzie, 1822): village community (mahal) as unit — North-Western Provinces (not NWFP), Punjab, Central India.
Revenue assessment under the British was high and rigid, causing indebtedness (UPSC 2012).

newNodesToCreate.title: Administrative Machinery — Civil Services, Judiciary & Police
prelimsNote: Cornwallis Code (1793): separation of revenue and judicial administration; Cornwallis is the 'father of the Indian Civil Services'.
Fort William College (1800, Wellesley) to train civil servants; Haileybury College (1806) in England.
Open competitive exam from 1853/1855; Satyendranath Tagore first Indian ICS (1863); Aitchison (1886), Islington, Lee Commission (1924) — Public Service Commission set up in 1926.
Police: Police Commission 1860 → Indian Police Act 1861; Police Commission 1902 (Curzon).
Butler Committee (1927) examined relations between the Paramount Power and the princely States (UPSC 2017).

newNodesToCreate.title: Education Policy & Institutions — From Calcutta Madrasa to the Sargent Plan
prelimsNote: Calcutta Madrasa (1781, Warren Hastings); Asiatic Society (1784, William Jones); Sanskrit College Benares (1791, Jonathan Duncan); Fort William College (1800, Richard — not Arthur — Wellesley); Sanskrit College was founded by Duncan, not William Jones (UPSC 2018).
Charter Act 1813 + General Committee of Public Instruction (1823) + Orientalist–Anglicist controversy → English education; Macaulay's Minute (1835) — UPSC 2018.
Wood's Despatch (1854): grants-in-aid, universities at Calcutta, Bombay, Madras (1857), vernacular at primary level — NOT English at all levels (UPSC 2018).
Hunter Commission (1882), Raleigh Commission & Indian Universities Act 1904 (Curzon), Sadler Commission (1917), Wardha Scheme (1937), Sargent Plan (1944).

newNodesToCreate.title: Colonial Foreign Policy & Integration of Princely States
prelimsNote: Anglo-Afghan Wars (1839–42, 1878–80, 1919); Forward Policy; Anglo-Burmese Wars (1824, 1852, 1885); Younghusband expedition to Tibet (1904).
Integration: Instrument of Accession and Standstill Agreements; Sardar Patel and V.P. Menon; Junagadh (plebiscite), Hyderabad (Operation Polo 1948), Kashmir (Oct 1947).
Post-1947 chronology (UPSC 2018) — e.g. first general elections 1951–52, linguistic reorganisation 1956.
Archaeologists Alexander Rea, Longhurst, Robert Sewell, James Burgess and Walter Elliot were associated with excavations (UPSC 2023).
